_note: Single source of truth for every number in the Stage 1 submission. Nulls and empty lists fail the gates, so nothing here survives as a placeholder, and a string in a numeric field fails too. Week 2 fills geometry, operating, performance, efficiency, the candidate and sensitivity tables, power_by_radius, mass_envelope_g and sources. Week 3 fills pitch, pitch_schedule, vector_map and packaging. Week 4 fills structure, mass_budget_g and the remaining results. Hard limits are checked against values RECOMPUTED from geometry and the mass lines, so an optimistic headline number achieves nothing. mass_envelope_g lines are {item, nominal_g, conservative_g, basis, scaling_class} with distinct item names. mass_budget_g lines are {item, mass_g, basis, refines}, where refines names the mass_envelope_g item this line came from, so week 4 continuity is checked per component and not only on the total. Aerodynamic power is bounded below by momentum theory over the declared momentum_area_m2, which may not exceed 2R times span, and the figure of merit that falls out has to be credible for a cyclorotor. thrust_sensitivity freezes in week 2 what raising thrust costs, and week 4 may only choose a row from it. Structural demands are derived: per-blade mass from the blade budget and blade count, rotor shaft torque from shaft power and speed, blade root bending from thrust per blade, lever arm and load factor. Row shapes for the remaining lists, so nothing sits in the schema without one: configuration_candidates {config, rotors, module_mass_g, thrust_N, module_tw, selected}, 3 or more; coefficient_scenarios {name, blade_area_coeff, basis, evidence_class}, 3 or more, where evidence_class is measured, derived or downside and a transferred value is never called measured; aero_azimuthal_loads {azimuth_deg, normal_force_N}, 24 or more; drive_candidates {name, continuous_power_W, continuous_torque_Nm, mass_g, selected}, 2 or more; linkage_dimensions {link, length_mm}, 4 or more; pitch_schedule {azimuth_deg, pitch_deg}, 24 or more; vector_map {phase_command_deg, vertical_force_N, lateral_force_N}, 3 or more. Every mass_envelope_g line also carries scaling_class, one of geometry, power or fixed, because the drive is not a fixed mass.

configuration_candidates.config: two rotors, 3 blades each, 85 mm radius
three rotors, 3 blades each, 70 mm radius

coefficient_scenarios.name: S2 quad rotor hover point, transferred
coefficient_scenarios.basis: 1.98 N per rotor on four NACA 0010 blades of 33.0 mm chord and 158.8 mm span at 76.2 mm radius and 2000 rpm, divided by the blade area dynamic pressure in this project's own area convention

coefficient_scenarios.name: S2 twin rotor, three blades at the same radius and speed
coefficient_scenarios.basis: 1.47 N per rotor on three blades of 25.4 mm chord and 152.4 mm span at 76.2 mm radius and 2000 rpm, recomputed the same way. Higher than the quad but at a solidity of 0.159, far outside the measured band, so it is carried as an upside indication and not adopted

coefficient_scenarios.name: blade deflection loss only
coefficient_scenarios.basis: the nominal transfer less a 5 percent thrust loss for blade bending and torsion, sized against the computed section stiffness rather than assumed

coefficient_scenarios.name: deflection loss and configuration transfer
coefficient_scenarios.basis: the nominal transfer less 5 percent for blade flexibility and a further 10 percent for a transfer that changes blade count, airfoil and chord ratio at once with nothing measured to de-risk it

drive_candidates.name: T-Motor Antigravity MN2806 KV650
drive_candidates.basis: supplier datasheet, 187 W and 12.3 A maximum continuous at 180 s; torque derived from 9.5493 over KV at the continuous current
drive_candidates.verdict: short of the 513 W the design point needs at the motor terminals

drive_candidates.name: T-Motor Navigator MN3110 KV470
drive_candidates.basis: supplier datasheet, 330 W and 15 A maximum continuous at 180 s, 98 g with leads; torque derived from 9.5493 over KV at the continuous current less the 0.3 A idle current
drive_candidates.verdict: covers the 13 N sensitivity row at 4 to 1 but not the 20 N design point

drive_candidates.name: T-Motor Navigator MN3510 KV700
drive_candidates.basis: supplier datasheet, 555 W and 25 A maximum continuous at 180 s, 118 g with leads; torque derived from 9.5493 over KV at the continuous current
drive_candidates.verdict: 513 W of the 555 W continuous rating and 21.7 A of the 25 A continuous current at 6 to 1, so it runs on its continuous rating and not its peak

mass_envelope_g.basis: PMI foam core at 52 kg/m3 filling 88 percent of the NACA 0020 section, two plies of 60 gsm carbon twill skin at 0.22 kg/m2 over a 2.05 chord perimeter, a CFRP spar tube of 0.12 chord diameter and 0.5 mm wall, bond line and two root fittings, times three blades
six CFRP spider arms of 14 by 1.5 mm section and radius length, two aluminium hub bosses and six blade attachment brackets
two miniature pitch bearings and one CFRP pitch link with rod ends per blade, plus an aluminium offset ring of 6 by 3 mm section on the rotor radius with its two support bearings and three pivots
CFRP through shaft of 14 mm diameter and 1 mm wall over the span, two steel stub adapters, two main bearings, and a drive end allowance of 18 g per newton metre of rotor torque
two bearing blocks, four CFRP frame tubes of 8 mm diameter and 1 mm wall spanning the rotor envelope, a motor mount plate and four airframe mount lugs
T-Motor Navigator MN3510 KV700, 555 W maximum continuous electrical power and 25 A maximum continuous current from the supplier datasheet, 118 g including leads
single stage HTD toothed belt reduction of 6 to 1: motor pulley, belt and tensioner hardware, with the rotor pulley rim mass following the torque it carries at 22 g per newton metre
one brushless controller rated above the motor 25 A continuous current, from the same catalogue class as the motor
two digital metal gear servos of the 12.5 g class driving the pitch offset direction against the residual pitch link load
pitch offset controller board at 8 g plus 17 g of silicone power and signal wiring routed over the module envelope
screws, threaded inserts, standoffs and structural adhesive at the frame, bearing and blade attachment joints

performance.blade_area_coeff: Benedict 2010 (S2), quad-cyclocopter rotor at hover, 1.98 N per rotor at 2000 rpm; recomputed here in the blade-area convention and labelled derived, never measured on this configuration
performance.blade_area_coeff_low: Engineering downside scenario, not a published bound. Kellen 2019 holds the measured coefficient for this shape family and is still behind a browser challenge, so nothing here is a measured lower limit
performance.momentum_area_m2: Projected frontal area 2R times span, the standard cyclorotor momentum closure and the cap the gate applies
performance.power_loading_ref_N_per_W: Benedict 2010 (S2) twin-cyclorotor at its operating point, 0.062 N/W of blade aerodynamic power, the lower of the two measured routes available
performance.blade_deflection_thrust_loss: Sized against the computed blade section: EI from the spar tube and skin, GJ from the closed cell, giving the tip deflection and twist reported in 02-rotor-sizing.md

thrust_sensitivity.drive_consequence: MN3110 KV470 at 330 W continuous covers it with the belt ratio dropped to 4 to 1
MN3510 KV700 at 555 W continuous, belt ratio 5 to 1, 17 A of the 25 A allowed
MN3510 KV700 at 555 W continuous, belt ratio 6 to 1, 22 A of the 25 A allowed
beyond the shortlist: 555 W continuous is exceeded and a heavier motor class is needed, which is why raising thrust stops paying here
